claims.text: The two groups show distinct attacker behaviors that can be directly compared using only the visible facts.

In Group 1 (source 183.62.140.253) each request targets a different invalid username, uses separate source ports (33521 and 33902), and ends with an immediate “Received disconnect … Bye Bye [preauth]” after the failed password attempt; this pattern repeats only twice within the sample window.

In Group 2 (source 187.141.143.180) every request attempts to authenticate as the same privileged user “root”, uses three distinct source ports (33314, 34508, 35685), and also terminates with a pre‑authentication disconnect after each failed password; however it contains six lines spanning roughly one minute.

The more anomalous attacker is the one in Group 2 because its consistent targeting of a high‑privilege account across multiple rapid attempts demonstrates a focused brute‑force strategy, whereas Group 1’s activity appears scattered and exploratory with no repeated credential focus.

Root‑cause hypothesis: both sources are likely compromised client machines running automated SSH‑brute‑force tools that have been misconfigured or deliberately scripted to probe for weak credentials; the differing patterns reflect variations in the attackers’ objectives — one may be testing a broad list of usernames, while the other is concentrating on high‑value accounts such as “root” to gain privileged access.
